title: Probability Distributions: The Shapes of Chance

questions.question: When rolling two fair dice, which total is most likely?
questions.rationale: Seven has six combinations (1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2, 6+1) — more than any other total, giving probability 6/36.

questions.question: For a fair die, the expected value of the face shown is:
questions.rationale: E(X) = (1+2+3+4+5+6)/6 = 3.5 — the long-run average, even though no single roll shows it.

questions.question: The binomial distribution models:
options: The number of successes in n independent trials with constant success probability
questions.rationale: Binomial counts successes across n independent trials, each with the same p — formula: C(n,k)·pᵏ·(1−p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ.

questions.question: Quadrant: a poll samples 1,000 voters. The standard error of the sample proportion shrinks roughly by what factor relative to the population spread?
questions.rationale: The standard error is σ/√n; with n = 1000 the factor is about 1/31.6, giving poll margins of error near ±3%.

questions.question: Which model best fits counting the number of typos on a random page of a book (rare events in a fixed interval)?
questions.rationale: Poisson models counts of rare events per unit of time or space — typos per page, calls per minute, defects per batch.
